messages:
lena: Quick architecture sync: proposal to allow a compact 'precision map' on requests so different submodules (early mlp, attention, heads) can use different precisions (fp8 / int8 / 4bit) without maintaining separate model binaries.

sam: Love the idea. main constraints? perf overhead for switching, validation cost at front-door, and ops safety.

lena: Exactly. Goals: (1) bounded validation cost (<1ms avg), (2) minimal kernel swaps (prefer contiguous ranges), (3) clear telemetry for quality drift. Not aiming for per-token routing yet.

rex: Implementation sketch: request carries list of ranges: [{start:0,end:6,prec:fp8,mode:soft},{start:7,end:-1,prec:4bit,mode:enforce}]. Worker merges adjacent same-prec ranges. Reject > 10 entries.

tara: Ops requirements: if mode=enforce and capacity missing -> either queue or reject. No silent fallback. Soft can fallback but must emit 'fallback_reason' including metric id.

lena: Telemetry fields we agreed: requested_map, applied_map, switch_count, fallback_reason (if any), sample_flag, prompt_id, deg_estimate. Minimal schema v0.1.

sam: Perf: measure switch penalty by counting wall-time delta when switch_count increases. add microbench: 0 switches, 1 switch, 3 switches.

ci-bot: Reminder: please add unit tests for coalesceRanges and validation limits before landing.

rex: SDK UX: add helper client.precisionMap(ranges) that validates contiguousness and trims redundant ranges. Also provide server-side canonicalizer.

tara: Rollout plan: shadow run for 1 week at 2% traffic -> opt-in beta -> 3 customer canaries -> full rollout with automatic rollback if deg_estimate > 4% for 30m.

lena: Action items: rex -> canonicalizer & unit tests; sam -> perf harness; tara -> canary playbook + alert thresholds; I'll draft RFC follow-up with telemetry schema. Check-in Friday.

ci-bot: CI job queued for canary infra. :gear:
